verdict: Ad spend is trickling, not scaling, and no lead or conversion data is coming back to prove the campaign works.
diagnosis: Spend collapsed to $3.85 on the latest day from a 28-day average of $13.63, suggesting the PCOS and postpartum campaign is stalling.

signals.headline: Total 28-day spend only $2,330
signals.detail: That is roughly $83 per day across the period, thin for a lead campaign meant to fill a studio pipeline.

signals.headline: Latest day spend dropped to $3.85
signals.detail: Down from the $13.63 daily average. Budget pacing or delivery has broken and needs a same-week check.

signals.headline: Zero lead data across 4 sources
signals.detail: No CRM, organic, local, or top-performer data reported this period. You cannot judge cost per lead without it.

signals.headline: 1 active campaign carrying everything
signals.detail: The PCOS and postpartum persona campaign is the only paid effort visible. No backup if it fatigues.

signals.headline: 346,446 impressions delivered this period
signals.detail: Reach is healthy relative to spend, but without lead tracking you cannot tell if the audience is converting.

recommendations.title: Fix lead tracking before adding budget
recommendations.detail: Connect the Facebook lead form to your CRM this week. Without lead counts, the $2,330 spent this period cannot be judged good or bad.

recommendations.title: Investigate why daily spend dropped to $3.85
recommendations.detail: Check budget caps, ad approval status, and audience delivery. A campaign spending 28% of its daily average is likely throttled or exhausted.

recommendations.title: Test a second creative angle before July costs climb
recommendations.detail: Fitness lead costs peak in July. Consider a second persona hook or a low-friction offer like a free class pass to keep cost per lead down.
